notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2022, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by county and city boards of education, which the Census counts as separate school systems, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($23,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Alabama county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Alabama yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Dallas County Sheriff's Department operates three Flock Safety automated license plate readers as of September 2025.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS017761, citing Public Records From the EFF via Pittsboro Police - See note

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Dallas County Sheriff's Office's Department operates one DJI Inspire drone as of 2016, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 1 Flock Safety license-plate camera is mapped inside City of Valley Grande's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
